headline: US and China propose AI hotline, but it won't be ready soon
summary: The US and China have proposed AI 'red lines' and a hotline for rapid communication and joint responses to rogue AI actions, as the two countries look for ways to manage AI-related national security risks. Wired reports the hotline system won't be ready for a while, even as the countries race for AI dominance.

claims.statement: The US and China have proposed a hotline to communicate on AI-related national security issues

sources.quote: US and China propose hotline to de-escalate AI threats ahead of Washington summit
the countries also appear to be figuring out ways to communicate on national security issues.

claims.statement: The proposed hotline would allow rapid communication and joint responses to rogue AI actions

sources.quote: The U.S. and China have proposed implementing AI red lines that will not be crossed, as well as a hotline between the two countries to provide rapid communication and opportunities for joint responses to rogue AI actions.

discrepancies.explanation: Wired frames the hotline as not imminent, while Tom's Hardware reports the proposal without noting a timeline.

quotes.quote: A US-China AI Hotline Won't Be Ready For a While
